newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura says IPOs may slow '97 Warsaw bourse growth.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says IPOs may slow '97 Warsaw bourse growth.

text.p: Large planned 1997 initial public offerings of copper firm KGHM Polska Miedz SA and Bank Handlowy SA could limit growth on the Warsaw bourse, Nomura Equity Research said in its January East European report.
Nomura said the offerings, estimated at $500 million and $300 respectively, could draw significant capital from stocks.

"The size of the issues...imply that there is only limited scope for price appreciation in existing shares as investors are likely to raise money by reducing some of their existing holdings," the report said.
Nomura said that the two firms, each likely to be valued at $1 billion-$2 billion, would significantly alter the composition of Warsaw's main WIG index.
It said the National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation programme could add another $1 billion to the market upon their planned listing in 1997's second quarter.
